observation: call_routine's ROM0/HOME-target path (address < 0x4000) sets PC directly and relies on returning to the injected 0x3FFF sentinel with no Bankswitch indirection. In this build 0x3FFF is ROM padding ($FF = RST 38), so the callee's own final ret unwinds into RST 38 -> $0038 and runs whatever unrelated real game code happens to be mapped there, instead of returning to the caller. The ROMX-target path is unaffected: Bankswitch's own .Return label is a real, always-mapped ROM0 address reached before the final ret pops 0x3FFF. Every existing call_routine usage in this suite targets a ROMX label, so this path was apparently never exercised - found 2026-08-27 porting _Divide (engine/math/multiply_divide.asm), where it silently returned a plausible-looking wrong result (no crash, no timeout, a repeating garbage pattern from an unrelated background call).
decision_needed: Either fix call_routine to route ROM0/HOME targets through Bankswitch too (bank=0 is safe: the fixed $0000-$3FFF region is unaffected by the bank-select write, so this gives both paths the same safe .Return hop) or explicitly document that call_routine must not be trusted for a ROM0/HOME target and callers should hook a label inside the routine instead of relying on its return.
test_boundary: Any call_routine(label) where label resolves to an address below $4000 is affected. All current test-suite usages (CriticalHitTest, ApplySingleBadgeStatBoost, AISelectSendOut, ProcPreloadAssignedWildArea, SaveGameData, LoadMainData) target ROMX and are unaffected.

observation: call_routine hijacks PC from wherever the CPU happens to be parked when the previous helper stopped ticking, and boot_fight2 stops the instant its MainInBattleLoop hook fires. That resume point is an accident of cycle timing, not a defined state, so any engine change that shifts when the battle loop is reached moves it. Measured 2026-09-01 with an AISelectSendOut change that makes the OPENING send-out skip the scored candidate scan (strictly less work, and behaviourally a no-op for this fixture): boot_fight2(seed=1) ended at frame 1583, PC=$211E, SP=$DFDB, bank $01 before the change and frame 1566, PC=$1435, SP=$DFDD, bank $02 after it. Battle state was byte-identical either way (same party species, same lead slot 0, same species/level/HP), zero symbols changed bank, and no RST 38 occurred during boot. But the three test_laundry_scope tests, which all call_routine immediately after boot_fight2, went from passing to a runaway RST 38 with SP walking down into VRAM ($91D7) - because PC was overwritten mid-routine in bank $02 instead of at the benign spot the old timing happened to produce. The ROM is not at fault; the fixture's implicit assumption is.
decision_needed: Give call_routine a defined entry state instead of inheriting an arbitrary one. Options: park the CPU at a known safe boundary before hijacking PC (e.g. tick to a hook on a known idle/loop label and only then set PC), or have boot_fight2 advance to a defined quiescent point after its MainInBattleLoop hook rather than stopping on the hook itself, or save/restore the full CPU state around call_routine so the interrupted context is not destroyed.
test_boundary: Affects every test that calls call_routine after boot_fight2 without an intervening save_state/load_state. Known affected: test_laundry_scope.LaundryScopeSmokeTest's three tests (hms field-move restriction, jessie_james fixed teams, move_swap audio state). Not a regression signal for engine changes: treat a new failure in these three after an unrelated battle-timing change as this contract until the battle state itself is shown to differ.
